def: The cumulative physiological wear and tear on the body and brain resulting from chronic, unmanaged stress exposure.
An event involving actual or threatened death, serious physical injury, sexual violation, or overwhelming terror that has the capacity to exceed immediate coping resources.
Predictable physiological and emotional tension arising from life demands, accompanied by natural autonomic activation and recovery.
Prolonged, unyielding hardships (poverty, discrimination, chronic illness) that strain reserves over time without a single discrete crisis.
The process by which an attuned, regulated caregiver calms and organizes a dysregulated nervous system through physical proximity, voice, and presence.
A physiological state characterized by blunted baseline cortisol levels paired with hypersensitive feedback receptors, frequently observed in chronic PTSD.
The optimal physiological and emotional zone where an individual can experience strong feelings and challenges while maintaining cognitive clarity and presence.
A state of sympathetic nervous system overdrive characterized by racing thoughts, panic, hypervigilance, insomnia, and irritability.
A state of parasympathetic/dorsal vagal collapse characterized by emotional numbness, detachment, exhaustion, freeze, and dissociation.
The sensory system through which the brain perceives internal bodily signals, including heartbeat, respiration, muscle tension, and visceral comfort.
The principle that memories are dynamically assembled upon recall using core sensory fragments, emotion, and current context rather than played back like a video recording.
Fragmented, uncontextualized sensory memory traces (flashes, smells, sounds) encoded during extreme stress when hippocampal time-stamping is disrupted.
An altered mental state involving persistent detachment from one's own physical body, emotions, or thoughts, as if observing oneself from outside.
An altered mental state where the external environment feels dreamlike, foggy, two-dimensional, artificial, or muffled behind glass.
A therapeutic model conceptualizing divisions between apparently normal parts of personality and emotional parts that manage trauma memories.
An ICD-11 diagnosis consisting of core PTSD symptoms plus Disturbances in Self-Organization (DSO): affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, and relational disturbances.
The three defining non-fear symptom clusters of ICD-11 Complex PTSD: chronic affect dysregulation, persistent negative self-concept, and relational impairment.
An influential proposed clinical framework capturing the cumulative impact of chronic childhood caregiver maltreatment; not yet codified in DSM-5-TR or ICD-11.
The principle that identical observable behaviors or symptoms can arise from radically different underlying psychological, biological, or environmental causes.
Psychological and existential distress resulting from actions, or lack thereof, that transgress an individual's deeply held moral code, ethics, or trust in authority.
Harm inflicted when an institution trusted to protect an individual causes harm, covers up abuse, or retaliates against reports of wrongdoing.
A state occurring when violence, oppression, or poverty is actively ongoing in the external environment, making hypervigilance an accurate survival response.
A trauma survival strategy where an individual seeks safety through appeasement, people-pleasing, and total suppression of personal boundaries.
A temporary period of enhanced synaptic plasticity and dendritic spine growth (often triggered by BDNF or ketamine) where new psychological patterns can be formed.
A first-line, guideline-supported cognitive-behavioral therapy involving gradual, safe therapeutic engagement with avoided memories and safe reminders.
A first-line, guideline-supported cognitive therapy helping clients examine and modify unhelpful trauma-related beliefs ('stuck points') regarding safety, trust, and guilt.
Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing; a structured first-line therapy using bilateral sensory stimulation while activating trauma memories.
An adult attachment status achieved when an individual with an insecure childhood history develops stable, secure relational patterns through healing relationships.
